title: Outlook mobile: Purview DLP wait-on-send for iOS and Android
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, commands and carefully qualified mobile documentation gaps are supported. Minor corrections should complete the two navigation paths, acknowledge the known baseline DLP licensing entitlement, and flag conflicting policy-tip guidance in a troubleshooting page.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans support for requiring DLP evaluation before email is sent from Outlook for iOS and Android.
claims.quote: Outlook for iOS and Android will support Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) wait-on-send policies. Organizations can require a DLP evaluation before an email is sent

claims.claim: DLPWaitOnSendEnabled enables evaluation before sending in new Outlook for Windows.
claims.quote: DLPWaitOnSendEnabled*boolean*: true or false.**Default**: false When true, it enables evaluation of the mail for Data loss prevention before mail is sent.

claims.claim: The documented default for DLPWaitOnSendEnabled in new Outlook is false.
claims.quote: DLPWaitOnSendEnabled*boolean*: true or false.**Default**: false

claims.claim: DLPWaitOnSendTimeout controls how long new Outlook waits for evaluation before offering override.
claims.quote: Specifies how long Outlook waits for DLP evaluation to complete before offering override.

claims.claim: The new Outlook Learn page prints a timeout range of 0 to 10,000 seconds.
claims.quote: DLPWaitOnSendTimeout*Integer*: range 0–10,000 seconds.

claims.claim: The documented timeout default is 9999 seconds.
claims.quote: A valid value is an integer from 0 to 9999. The default value is 9999.

claims.claim: The Set-OrganizationConfig reference instead gives a valid timeout range of 0 to 9999 seconds.
claims.quote: The DLPWaitOnSendTimeout parameter specifies how long in seconds Outlook for Windows waits for data loss prevention (DLP) evaluation to complete on a new message before offering an override. A valid value is an integer from 0 to 9999.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: In new Outlook, a timeout of 1 to 9998 seconds permits override after the specified wait.
claims.quote: A value from 1 to 9998 means Outlook waits for the specified number of seconds before it allows the user to override and send the message without completing DLP evaluation.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: In new Outlook, timeout 0 immediately exposes Send Anyway.
claims.quote: When DLPWaitOnSendTimeout = 0, user will immediately see “Send Anyway” in the infobar of mail.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: In new Outlook, timeout 9999 prevents sending until DLP evaluation completes.
claims.quote: The value 9999 means the user can't send the message unless the DLP evaluation is complete.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Policies reaches the policy list used for the oversharing rule and dialog control.

claims.fix: Extend the path to 'Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom (Categories) > Custom (Regulations) > Full directory (Admin units) > Exchange email > Define policy settings > Create or customize advanced DLP rules > Create rule > User notifications > On > Policy tips > Show the policy tip as a dialog for the end user before send (available for Exchange workload only)'. claims.claim: New-DlpComplianceRule -Name <rule name> -Policy <policy name> -NotifyUser Owner -NotifyPolicyTipDisplayOption Dialog -ContentContainsSensitiveInformation <label conditions> creates a rule with label conditions and the dialog policy-tip option.
claims.quote: New-DlpComplianceRule -Name <DLP Rule Name> -Policy <DLP Policy Name> -NotifyUser Owner -NotifyPolicyTipDisplayOption "Dialog" -ContentContainsSensitiveInformation @(@{operator = "And"; groups = @(@{operator="Or";name="Default";labels=@(@{name=<Label GUID>;type="Sensitivity"})})})
